Semantic-Space Exploration and Exploitation in RLVR for LLM Reasoning Fanding Huang*, Guanbo Huang*, Xiao Fan, Yi He, Xiao Liang, Xiao Chen, Qinting Jiang, Faisal Nadeem Khan, Jingyan Jiang†, Zhi Wang†. Accepted as ACL 2026 Findings. [Paper] [Code] [Project] [BibTex] Abstract

Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) for LLM reasoning is often framed as balancing exploration and exploitation in action space, typically operationalized with token-level proxies (e.g., output entropy or confidence). We argue that this apparent trade-off is largely a measurement artifact: token-level statistics reflect next-token uncertainty rather than how reasoning progresses over multi-token semantic structures. We therefore study exploration and exploitation in the hidden-state space of response trajectories. We use Effective Rank (ER) to quantify representational exploration and introduce its temporal derivatives, Effective Rank Velocity (ERV) and Effective Rank Acceleration (ERA), to characterize exploitative refinement dynamics. Empirically and theoretically, ER and ERV exhibit near-zero correlation in semantic space, suggesting the two capacities can be improved simultaneously. Motivated by this, we propose Velocity-Exploiting Rank Learning (VERL), which shapes the RL advantage with an auxiliary signal derived from ER/ERV and uses the more stable ERA as a meta-control variable to adaptively balance the incentives. Across multiple base models, RL algorithms, and reasoning benchmarks, VERL yields consistent improvements, including large gains on challenging tasks (e.g., 21.4% in Gaokao 2024).

MoETTA: Test-Time Adaptation Under Mixed Distribution Shifts with MoE-LayerNorm Xiao Fan, Jingyan Jiang†, Zhaoru Chen, Fanding Huang, Xiao Chen, Qinting Jiang, Bowen Zhang, Xing Tang, Zhi Wang. Accepted by AAAI 2026 (CCF-A, 17.6% overall acceptance rate). [Paper] [Code] [BibTex] [Poster] Abstract

Test-Time Adaptation (TTA) has proven effective in mitigating performance drops under single-domain distribution shifts by updating model parameters during inference. However, real-world deployments often involve mixed distribution shifts, where test samples are affected by diverse and potentially conflicting domain factors, posing significant challenges even for state-of-the-art TTA methods. A key limitation in existing approaches is their reliance on a unified adaptation path, which fails to account for the fact that optimal gradient directions can vary significantly across different domains. Moreover, current benchmarks focus only on synthetic or homogeneous shifts, failing to capture the complexity of real-world heterogeneous mixed distribution shifts. To address this, we propose MoETTA, a novel entropy-based TTA framework that integrates the Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture. Rather than enforcing a single parameter update rule for all test samples, MoETTA introduces a set of structurally decoupled experts, enabling adaptation along diverse gradient directions. This design allows the model to better accommodate heterogeneous shifts through flexible and disentangled parameter updates. To simulate realistic deployment conditions, we introduce two new benchmarks: potpourri and potpourri+. While classical settings focus solely on synthetic corruptions (i.e., ImageNet-C), potpourri encompasses a broader range of domain shifts—including natural, artistic, and adversarial distortions—capturing more realistic deployment challenges. Additionally, potpourri+ further includes source-domain samples to evaluate robustness against catastrophic forgetting. Extensive experiments across three mixed distribution shifts settings show that MoETTA consistently outperforms strong baselines, establishing new state-of-the-art performance and highlighting the benefit of modeling multiple adaptation directions via expert-level diversity.

docs.title: Campus Beamer
docs.text:
A clean, elegant, agent-oriented Beamer template for academic presentations. Turn an outline and prepared research materials into consistently typeset PDF and PowerPoint slides, with speaker notes and reusable TeX source.

GitHub Download releases Usage guide

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text:
An agent can produce a deck quickly, but a directly generated presentation may have inconsistent typography, weak academic structure, and references that are difficult to verify or reuse. Campus Beamer gives the agent a stable layout system and gives the author an inspectable source that can be revised and carried into future talks.

The workflow starts with the argument and supporting material. An expanded outline is reviewed before slides are generated; shared Beamer layouts then keep typography, navigation, citations, and speaker notes consistent.

docs.title: Six themes, one workflow
docs.text:
The default General theme uses a black-and-white palette, an original graduation-cap emblem, and the Campus Beamer wordmark. The same presentation structure can also use Tokyo Night, EVA, undefined, Tsinghua University, or Peng Cheng Laboratory themes.

General · Black and white

Tokyo Night · Dark palette

EVA · Red and black

undefined · Yellow palette

Tsinghua University

Peng Cheng Laboratory

Click any preview to enlarge it. Both 16:9 and 4:3 formats are supported. These are community project themes, not official institutional templates; theme assets retain their respective sources and usage terms.

docs.title: Built for research talks
docs.text:
Shared layouts support equations, code, figures, callouts, paper citations, progressive reveals, and navigation. The examples below show the English General theme.

Equations and structured layouts

Code presentation

Linked paper citations

Figures alongside text
  • PDF and PowerPoint. LaTeX handles typesetting; the default PPTX preserves slide appearance as rendered images, with links, embedded video, and speaker notes.
  • Native speaker notes. Notes are authored in TeX and exported to PowerPoint; a separate PDF layout can place notes beside each slide.
  • Traceable references. Literature tools help retrieve DBLP BibTeX entries and citation-count snapshots for verification.
  • Reusable source and themes. Revise the outline and TeX source for the next talk, or create a theme with its own palette and assets.

Experimental editable export

The current main branch also provides make pptx-editable for editable text, footers, and callouts. Emblems can be moved or replaced independently; equations and other complex content remain images, and recipients need the corresponding fonts. This is distinct from the default image-based PPTX export. See the editable export guide.

docs.title: From outline to slides
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository or unpack a release, then open it in an agent that can read local files and run commands.
  2. Run make init, fill in outline.md, and place papers, figures, and results in materials/.
  3. Ask the agent to create the presentation. Review its expanded outline before slide generation.
  4. Let the agent arrange the slides and notes, check the layout, and export PDF and PPTX.

Local workflows include environment checks and page previews, with Docker setup and an Overleaf import package also documented. See installation and workflow options for requirements and limitations.

The latest stable release provides ready-made examples and source downloads. The repository documents ongoing development.
